title: Make Costs of Paths Equal in a Binary Tree
statement: A perfect binary tree has `n` nodes labelled 1 to `n`: node 1 is the root, and every node `i` that is not a leaf has children `2 * i` and `2 * i + 1` (all leaves sit on the same, deepest level). Node `i` carries the value `cost[i - 1]`. The cost of a root-to-leaf path is the sum of the values of the nodes on it. One operation adds 1 to the value of a single node of your choice. Return the fewest operations needed so that every root-to-leaf path has the same cost.
notes:
## Intuition

Increments can only raise paths, so every path must end up at least as heavy as the heaviest one; the question is where to spend the increments. Look at two sibling leaves: whatever happens above them adds the same amount to both of their paths, so their difference `|left - right|` must be paid on the lighter leaf itself, and nothing cheaper exists. After that the two leaves act like one value, `max(left, right)`, that can be folded into their parent. Repeating this from the bottom of the tree turns every subtree into a single number: the heaviest path cost inside it. A top-down version, which computes each subtree's heaviest path and gives each node the slack it is missing, reaches the same total more slowly.

## Approach

1. Copy `cost` into `path`; `path[i]` will hold the heaviest path cost below node `i + 1`.
2. Visit each parent from the last one, `floor(n / 2)`, back to the root. Its children (1-based `2 * parent` and `2 * parent + 1`) are at indices `2 * parent - 1` and `2 * parent`.
3. Pay `|left - right|` to lift the lighter child's subtree to the heavier one.
4. Add `max(left, right)` to the parent's own value.
5. Return the total `increments`.

## Example 1, step by step

`cost = [1, 5, 2, 2, 3, 3, 1]`. Parent 3 has children with values 3 and 1: pay 2, and node 3 becomes `2 + 3 = 5`. Parent 2 has children 2 and 3: pay 1, and node 2 becomes `5 + 3 = 8`. The root has children 8 and 5: pay 3. The total is `2 + 1 + 3 = 6`, and every path costs `1 + 8 = 9`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every node except the root is folded into its parent once.
- Space: O(n) for the `path` copy (O(1) if `cost` may be overwritten).

## Pitfalls

- `cost` is 0-indexed while nodes are 1-based: node `i`'s children sit at indices `2i - 1` and `2i`.
- Pay the difference at the lowest level where it appears; lifting a parent instead raises both subtrees and is never cheaper.
- Fold the maximum, not the sum, of the two children into the parent.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | heaviest path cost below each node, filled from the bottom up |
| `increments` | operations paid so far |
| `parent` | 1-based label of the node whose children are being matched |
| `left`, `right` | heaviest path costs of its two subtrees |

narration.3: Copy the costs so the input stays untouched; each entry will grow into a subtree's heaviest path.
narration.4: No operations have been paid yet.
narration.5: Visit parents from the deepest one back to the root, so children are always finished first.
narration.6: Heaviest path through the left child (1-based node 2 * parent).
narration.7: Heaviest path through the right child (node 2 * parent + 1).
narration.8: Lift the lighter subtree to match the heavier one, right at the child.
narration.9: Both subtrees now share the heavier cost; fold it into the parent.
narration.11: Every pair of siblings is balanced; return the total paid.
